meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'A fear of weapons is a sign of retarded sexual and emotional maturity'?
meta.ogDescription: Freud never wrote this. It’s a distorted epigram from Don B. Kates Jr.’s 1990 gun-control essay, wrongly pinned on Freud.

answer.label: Not Sigmund Freud — a distorted paraphrase of a 1990 gun-rights essay
answer.authorName: Don B. Kates Jr. (his sentence, inverted)
answer.authorDates: Textual root: 1990 · falsely dated to Freud (1856–1939)
answer.sourceLine: This sentence appears in no translation of any work by Freud. It is an anonymous internet epigram compressed and inverted from a line in the gun-rights lawyer Don B. Kates Jr.’s 1990 monograph “Guns, Murders, and the Constitution,” where Kates actually wrote that Freud “associates retarded sexual and emotional development … with fear and loathing of weapons.” Freud himself never phrased it as a maxim; the pithy “quote” is a later fabrication.

source.heading: Where the line really comes from

docMeta.dd: Misattributed — fabricated paraphrase, in no Freud work
Don B. Kates Jr., “Guns, Murders, and the Constitution” (1990)

source.excerpt: “A fear of weapons is a sign of retarded sexual and emotional maturity.” — the viral form pinned on Freud. What Kates actually wrote in 1990: “Freud associates retarded sexual and emotional development not with gun ownership, but … with fear and loathing of weapons.”
trail: Wikiquote ↗ lists the line under “Misattributed,” noting it is found in no translation of any Freud work and traces to Kates’s 1990 essay.
Kates’s essay itself — archived at GunCite ↗ — contains the real sentence about “fear and loathing of weapons,” but NOT the pithy “A fear of weapons is a sign of…” maxim.
A dedicated Freud-quote investigation ↗ shows the maxim is an out-of-context adaptation of Kates, and quotes the genuine Freud line on the penis-as-weapon from “Dreams in Folklore.”
source.excerptNote: The gun-rights epigram compresses and hardens Kates’s cautious gloss into a maxim, then attributes it to Freud — who framed weapon-symbolism as neurotic phobia, never as a one-line aphorism.

sourceLink.text: Don B. Kates Jr., "Guns, Murders, and the Constitution" (1990), archived text

source.rightsNote: The exact aphorism has no identifiable authored source — it is an anonymous internet paraphrase, so no copyright status can be asserted for it. Its textual root, Kates’s 1990 monograph, is itself in-copyright, and the Freud passage it distorts comes from the 1958 English translation of “Dreams in Folklore” (also in-copyright), but neither is the verbatim source of the viral line.

author.name: Don B. Kates Jr.
author.heading: The lawyer whose sentence became a fake Freud quote
author.metaLine: American criminologist & gun-rights constitutional lawyer · d. 2016
author.bio: Don B. Kates Jr. was an American criminologist and civil-liberties lawyer who became one of the most-cited academic advocates of the individual-right reading of the Second Amendment. In his 1990 monograph Guns, Murders, and the Constitution, he cited Freud to argue that psychoanalysis linked retarded emotional development to fear of weapons, not to owning them. Internet users later compressed and inverted his careful gloss into a snappy maxim and pinned it on Freud himself.

misattribution.heading: A paraphrase promoted to a Freud quotation
misattribution.intro: This is a textbook manufactured quote: a scholar’s cautious gloss on Freud, hardened into an aphorism and re-labeled with a more famous name.

items.why: The maxim “A fear of weapons is a sign of retarded sexual and emotional maturity” appears in no translation of any Freud work ↗. It is an anonymous compression of a different sentence.

Kates actually wrote that Freud “associates retarded sexual and emotional development not with gun ownership, but … with fear and loathing of weapons” in his 1990 essay ↗ — a hedged interpretation, not a Freud quotation.

In Dreams in Folklore Freud described the penis represented “as a weapon, cutting knife, dagger” underlying “numerous phobias in neurotic people” — symbolism, not a verdict on gun attitudes, per the quote investigation ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: Freud never wrote this line; it is an internet paraphrase of gun-rights lawyer Don Kates’s 1990 gloss on Freud, as Wikiquote documents ↗.

context.heading: Why the fake stuck
lead: The sentence spread because it is rhetorically useful: it lets gun-rights advocates diagnose their opponents’ motives while borrowing the authority of the most famous name in psychology. The irony is that its literal meaning — that fearing weapons signals immaturity — is closer to what Freud’s interpreter Kates argued than to anything Freud declared outright.

Freud did write about weapons as dream-symbols for the penis, tied to the anxiety dreams and phobias of neurotic patients. But that clinical observation about symbolism is a long way from a one-line put-down about people who dislike guns.
context.pull: A scholar’s hedge became a celebrity’s slogan.
